title: 最大功率传输：转电位器，找功率最大的点
summary: 上一个实验的网络接一个可调负载：负载太小电压没了，太大电流没了，中间某处功率最大。
concepts: maximum power transfer 最大功率传输
description: 最大功率传输：负载电阻等于网络的戴维宁电阻（R_L = R_Th）时，负载得到的功率最大，P_max = V_Th² / (4R_Th)。这时效率最多 50%。

cards.title: 电压和电流在拔河
text: 搭上一个实验的网络（`9 V`、**R1**、**R2**、**R3** 接到端子 **T**）。从 T 出发，电流表 **AM1** 接到电位器 **RV1** `2.2 kΩ` 当可调负载：**中间脚和 3 脚连在一起**，接 GND。
**慢慢把 RV1** 从 `0%` 转到 `100%`。看电流表，再用万用表看 RV1 两端的电压。
`0%` 时电流很大、电压为零；`100%` 时正好反过来。功率 = 电压 × 电流。它在哪里最大？

cards.title: 负载和内阻一样大时，功率最大
text: - 对负载来说，网络就是 $V_{Th}$ 串 $R_{Th}$（上一个实验）。电流 $= V_{Th}/(R_{Th} + R_L)$，负载得到 $P = I^2R_L$。
- $R_L$ 很小：电流大，电压几乎没有；$R_L$ 很大：电压有了，电流几乎没有。乘积在中间最大，就在 $R_L = R_{Th}$ 处：
![](fig:peak)
- 峰很平：负载是 $R_{Th}$ 的一半或两倍，功率仍有最大值的约 89%。用上一个实验的 $R_{Th}$ 预测旋钮的位置。

cards.title: 三个位置，算三个功率
text: - 每次**测 RV1 两端的电压**（1 脚对 GND），**读 AM1**，再相乘：$P = V × I$。
- 电路检查通过后，填 `53%` 和 `100%` 两个位置的测量题。

cards.title: 带走
text: - **最大功率传输**：$R_L = R_{Th}$，这时 $P_{max} = V_{Th}^2 / (4R_{Th})$。
- 峰值时负载和 $R_{Th}$ 平分功率：效率最多 50%。这里真实的 9 V 电源效率更低——等效电路只对外等效，和 2.3 一样。
- 电网要效率，负载远大于 $R_{Th}$；无线电、音响、传感器要的是信号最大，所以讲究**匹配**。
- 坑：匹配时电池自己和负载一样发热。直接短路更糟：功率全部烧在电池里面。

caption.text: 负载功率随 R_L 变化：R_L = R_Th 时最大，两边下降得很慢。

i18n.en: Load power against R_L: it peaks at R_L = R_Th and falls off slowly on both sides.

en.title: Maximum power transfer: turn the pot, find the peak
en.summary: The network from the last lab drives an adjustable load: too small and the voltage vanishes, too large and the current does; the power peaks in between.
en.description: Maximum power transfer: a load gets the most power when its resistance equals the network's Thévenin resistance (R_L = R_Th); then P_max = V_Th² / (4R_Th), at no more than 50 % efficiency.
en.compare:
**Compare**: the peak is at **R_L = R_Th**: P_max = V_Th² / (4R_Th) = 6.19² / 4632 ≈ **8.27 mW**.
- 25% (R_L = 550 Ω): V ≈ 1.99 V, I ≈ 3.62 mA, P ≈ **7.2 mW**.
- 53% (R_L ≈ 1166 Ω ≈ R_Th): V ≈ 3.10 V, I ≈ 2.66 mA, P ≈ **8.27 mW** (the peak).
- 100% (R_L = 2.2 kΩ): V ≈ 4.05 V, I ≈ 1.84 mA, P ≈ **7.5 mW**.

**Efficiency**: in the equivalent circuit the load and R_Th share the peak power equally, 50 %. The real circuit needs its own sum: at 53% the 9 V source delivers 4.64 mA, i.e. 41.8 mW, and only 8.27 mW (about 20 %) reaches the load.

measurements.ask: Knob at `53%`: load voltage V (RV1 pin 1 to GND)
Knob at `53%`: load power P = V × I (from your readings)
Knob at `100%`: load power P = V × I
measurements.explain: R_L = 2.2 kΩ ≈ 1.9 R_Th: only about 10 % below the peak.

choices: The larger R_L the better: largest at 100%
The smaller R_L the better: largest near 0%
measurements.ask: Compare your powers (try more positions if you like): where is P largest?
measurements.explain: P peaks at R_L = R_Th, P_max = V_Th² / (4R_Th). The peak is gentle: twice or half R_Th costs only about 10 %.

hints: First build the last lab's network (R1, R2, R3); the terminal is R3's far end, T.
Ammeter red lead on T, black lead on the pot's pin 1; join the pot's middle pin and pin 3 and take them to GND.
At 0% the load is 0 (a short); at 100% it is 2.2 kΩ.

cards.title: Voltage and current in a tug of war
text: Build the network from the last lab (`9 V`, **R1**, **R2**, **R3** to terminal **T**). From T, the ammeter **AM1** feeds the pot **RV1** `2.2 kΩ` as a variable load: **join its middle pin to pin 3** and take them to GND.
**Turn RV1 slowly** from `0%` to `100%`. Watch the ammeter, and the voltage across RV1 with the multimeter.
At `0%` there is plenty of current but no voltage; at `100%` it is the other way round. The power is voltage × current. Where is it largest?

cards.title: The power peaks when the load matches the inner resistance
text: - To the load, the network is just $V_{Th}$ in series with $R_{Th}$ (last lab). The current is $V_{Th}/(R_{Th} + R_L)$, and the load gets $P = I^2R_L$.
- A tiny $R_L$ takes a big current but almost no voltage; a huge $R_L$ takes the voltage but almost no current. The product peaks in between, at $R_L = R_{Th}$:
- Example, a 9 V battery ($R_{Th}$ = 1.5 Ω): a 1.5 Ω load gets $9^2 / (4 × 1.5) = 13.5$ W — and the battery burns the same 13.5 W inside itself.
![](fig:peak)
- The peak is flat: half or twice $R_{Th}$ still gives about 89 % of the maximum. Use the $R_{Th}$ from the last lab to predict the knob position.

cards.title: Three positions, three powers
text: - Turn RV1 to `25%`, `53%` and `100%` (more positions if you like).
- Each time, **measure the voltage across RV1** (pin 1 to GND) and **read AM1**, then multiply: $P = V × I$.
- Once the circuit check passes, fill in the questions for `53%` and `100%`.

cards.title: Take away
text: - **Maximum power transfer**: $R_L = R_{Th}$, and then $P_{max} = V_{Th}^2 / (4R_{Th})$.
- At the peak the load and $R_{Th}$ share the power equally: 50 % efficiency at best. Here the real 9 V source does even worse — the equivalent is only equal outside, as in 2.3.
- Power grids want efficiency, so their loads are far larger than $R_{Th}$. Radio, audio and sensor circuits want the most signal, so they **match**.
- Pitfall: a matched battery heats up as much as its load. Shorting a battery is worse: all the power stays inside.

旋钮在 `53%`：电流 I（AM1 的读数）
旋钮在 `53%`：负载功率 P = V × I（用你的读数算）

measurements.explain: R_L = 2.2 kΩ ≈ 1.9 R_Th：功率只比峰值少约 10%。

choices: R_L 越大越好：100% 时最大
R_L 越小越好：越接近 0% 越大

measurements.explain: R_L = R_Th 时 P 最大，P_max = V_Th² / (4R_Th)。峰很平缓：R_L 偏离 R_Th 一倍，P 也只少约 10%。
